trial.description: one variant scored on one case: whether the fact the case's agent lacked was in front of it, unasked, before it erred, and whether a search with the words it was answering finds it. Its eid is derived from the case and the variant, so a rerun replaces the score

case.description: the entity wearing miss{entry, needed, across, told}

variant.description: the persona whose context was assembled

unasked.description: the case's needed entity was among what the variant put in front of the agent before its entry: the persona, the compaction summary, notices, knocks delivered and hit rows returned. Its own searches and a pointer from a person do not count

asked.description: a search with the words of the message the agent was answering (its first twelve words) returns the needed entity among its first five rows that predate the entry

tokens.description: the size of what the variant put in front of the agent, at four characters a token

round.description: one round of a skill trial: attempts at cases under variants, the pairs a person compares and the judges' scores, read back to plan the next round. Its title is its `doc`

skill.description: the name of the skill the round develops, `copywriting`; a round file's variants and cases are named under it (`variant:copywriting:none`)

parts.description: the names of the parts every attempt returns, in the order a page draws them: `["headline", "brief", "description"]`

variant.description: a candidate text of a skill, handed to a writer in a skill trial and installed nowhere. Its title is its `doc`; it is kept out of search and embedding so no agent meets it unasked

body.description: the text handed to the writer; empty for the control that gets no skill

theory.description: one line: what this variant believes makes the work good

source.description: where the text came from when it was not written here: a URL, or `path@sha`

licence.description: the licence the source gives the text under

from.description: the variant this one was changed from, in a later round

case.description: what a writer in a skill trial is handed to work on: a brief, or (wearing `riddle`) a fact sheet. Its title is its `doc`

body.description: the text the writer is handed

base.description: the case this one adds input to (the same facts plus the owner's words): two cases with one base are about one thing, so their attempts can be compared

riddle.description: on a case: the writer describes a named thing from its fact sheet without naming it, and a judge who sees only the attempt guesses what it is

aliases.description: other guesses that count as right

forbidden.description: substrings an attempt may not contain, in any case

forbidden_exact.description: whole words an attempt may not contain, case-sensitive

group.description: the cluster of similar things it sits in; a judge choosing `among` sees the group's fact sheets

found.description: on a case: something its maker published themselves (a first home page, a launch post), found and kept to learn a judge's taste. Its one attempt holds the text with the name masked in `output` and the original in `reply`, and a page showing it says nothing that names it

source.description: where it was read: a URL

attempt.description: what one writer returned for one case in a skill trial. A model's attempt names its variant, persona, run and model, and wears `usage` and `cost`; a person's own attempt names only its round and case, and its writer is its `created.by`

round.description: the round it was written in

case.description: the case the writer was handed

variant.description: the skill text the writer was handed; absent on a person's own attempt

persona.description: the persona the writer carried; absent when it carried none (a blank model)

run.description: which of the repeated runs of the same case, variant and persona

reply.description: everything the writer said, its working included

output.description: the work itself, by the round's `parts`: `{headline, brief, description}`

pair.description: two attempts a person is asked to compare, planned by whoever ran the round. Which is shown first is the page's to shuffle

round.description: the round whose deck it is in

preference.description: one comparison of two attempts by its writer (`created.by`): which they would rather read on from, or neither. One row per judge and pair; choosing again changes it

chose.description: the one preferred; absent when neither was

why.description: a few words of why, when the judge gave any

grabbed.description: its writer (`created.by`) found this attempt appealing on its own, whatever it was compared with. Deleting the row takes the mark back

guess.description: one judge's guesses at what a riddle attempt describes, having seen only the attempt

form.description: `open`: the judge lists guesses in order; `among`: the judge also sees the fact sheets of the case's group and picks

among.description: the choices it was shown, in the `among` form

rank.description: the 1-based place of the right answer among its guesses; absent when it was not within `cap`

cap.description: how many guesses it was allowed

leaked.description: forbidden strings found in the attempt, which give the answer away

trial_tally.title: Tally a round of a skill trial
trial_tally.description: Print what a round's rows say: for each variant, persona arm and case, how often its attempts were preferred, how often neither was, and how many grabbed the judge; the judges' mean guesses until right; and whether the two agree. Reads only.

round.description: the round: its key as loaded (`copy-r1`), its id or its eid
